data.narrative:
d-Matrix is a Series A semiconductor company that has raised $450M against a current post-money valuation of $2.0B. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductor names (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private frontier-chip firms including SambaNova Systems, Rebellions, and Cerebras.

Two methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $4.0B. Peer-median anchoring across 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—SambaNova ($11.0B), Rebellions ($2.3B), and Positron AI ($1.0B)—produces a median of $2.3B. Public-comp P/S anchoring cannot be applied; the public semiconductor median sits at 20.5x, but d-Matrix's revenue is not disclosed. Revenue disclosure would unlock this method and potentially tighten the range.

The two applicable methods triangulate to a valuation range of $2.0B (low) to $4.6B (high), with a median of $3.2B. The current $2.0B post-money sits at the lower bound, consistent with peer-median but conservative relative to stage-progression norms. Key uncertainties include d-Matrix's revenue trajectory relative to peers, the severity of commercialization risk in advanced chip design, and whether the SambaNova outlier ($11.0B) reflects sustainable market pricing or exuberance. Additional disclosure on revenue run rate and customer traction would refine this range materially.
